claim: A floor or ceiling texel is 16 map units (8 with floorstat/ceilingstat bit 3, 'double smooshiness'), and unless bit 6 (relative alignment) is set the pattern is laid on the map's own grid. Moving a sector by anything but a whole number of its tile's period (pixels x 16) shifts its floor pattern; a 64-pixel crate tile covers 1,024 units, a 128-pixel one 2,048.
evidence: NBlood/source/build/src/engine.cpp:2797-2799 (calc_globalshifts) globalxshift from the tile's size, one more with globalorientation&8
NBlood/source/build/include/buildtypes.h:24 bit 3 double smooshiness; :27 bit 6 align texture to first wall
use: Size floor-textured modules from the art (pixels x 16); translate geometry only by whole periods (Gravesend's release shift is (-131,072, -16,384): each a whole number of 16,384, four of its longest tile's period, and on the 1,024 plan grid).

checked.how: engine.cpp:2795-2799 read (calc_globalshifts): globalxshift = 8 - log2 width, globalyshift likewise, one more each when globalorientation&8. buildtypes.h:20-27 ceilingstat/floorstat comment: bit 3 'double smooshiness' at :24, bit 6 'Align texture to first wall' at :27. release.py:34-36: SHIFT = (-128*1024, -16*1024) = (-131,072, -16,384), PERIOD 16,384 - the shift is not '16,384' alone; use corrected.
